A better understanding of the quantified hosting capacity resulting from different methods showcases their point of improvement and facilitates the election of the quantification method.

articleTitle: In brief Recent Background, Challenges, and Strategies for Electrified Aircraft Development
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Electrified aircraft and flying vehicles are the future of aviation, and society’s transportation. These technologies have emerged as a key enabling technology for concepts ranging from hybrid-electric propulsion systems to all-electric aircraft. So, this paper reviews some recent advanced samples for related research premises/hypotheses to electrified airplanes. It presents a brief overview of the background, and challenges, along with electric aircraft architectures, design, enabling technology, commercial aircraft programs, storage, powertrain, charging systems, auxiliary power units, power converters, and future trends. Finally, the paper presents some important tips, and recommendations for future research directions.

articleTitle: Grade Crossing Incidents: A Probability Analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: We analyze five railroad grade crossings in California, exploring the issue of collision likelihood and overall risk of incident. Crossings analyzed include Grape Street in San Diego, Rosecrans-Marquardt in Santa Fe Springs, Cutting Boulevard in Richmond, Bellevue Avenue in Atwater, and Grand Avenue in Carlsbad. Multiple sources estimating the number of collisions by crossing per year are discussed, as well as explanation of the methodologies involved and their possible shortcomings. Images collected from Google Maps are shared in order to better represent each crossing and the surrounding geographical features that help to define them. We also used information from the California Department of Transportation (Caltrans), the Federal Railroad Administration (FRA), and the United States Department of Transportation (DOT) [1, 2, 3]. These were sources for our defining key statistical parameters of each of the crossings, approximations of the number of collisions per year, and actual collision history at each crossing. Potential solutions and technologies that may serve to better mitigate and eliminate risk to human life and property are also presented.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Wireless Sensor Monitoring System to Combat Underground Copper Cable Theft
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: An enhanced low-cost ultra wideband omnidirectional antenna to optimise the function of the entire underground Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) is designed to help combat underground copper cable theft. To evaluate the proposed solution, two 3D electromagnetic computers, allowing the allowing network simulation of the WSNs antennas using High-Frequency Structure Simulator Software (Ansys HFSS). In addition, Ansys HFSS was used to perform numerical simulation in order to evaluate the efficiency of the proposed Square Slotted Monopole Antenna (SSMA) with that of traditional directional antennas called Circular Monopole Antenna with Slots (CMAS). The simulation results proved that the proposed SSMA antennas design has a high-frequency depth, increased dispersion of the transmitted signals as well as their spreading. For a depth of 30 cm, the results obtained have shown an average fidelity of 0.9 and a spreading factor of 1.5, which is higher than the traditional CMAS, which obtained less than 1 spread factor and less than 1.7 fidelity.

articleTitle: Analysis of Lifestyle Habits from Weblogs of Patients with Intractable Diseases Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: In recent years, patient-centered medicine has become widely accepted. To keep a record of their struggles, patients sometimes publish their diaries (disease blogs) on weblogs to be read by an unspecified number of people. In particular, writing a blog may be helpful in the case of intractable diseases of which there are few cases, and patients often feel isolated because they know few people with the same disease. In this study, we used deep learning technology to analyze the blogs written by patients with intractable diseases and to determine how they live their daily lives and their feelings. If their lifestyles are understood, the relationship between the physical condition and mental changes of people fighting intractable diseases can be determined, and a system that shows behavioral guidelines for new users fighting similar intractable diseases can be built.

articleTitle: Cost-Effective High-Speed SRM Drive with Simple Hall-Effect Position Sensors and Minimized Number of Power Switches
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: In this paper, a cost-effective switched reluctance motor (SRM) for high-speed applications is proposed. First, SRM is widely known to have relatively low manufacturing costs because of its simplistic design and structure. Generally, SRM with lower phase numbers is used for high-speed application and thus a 2-phase SRM is selected in this paper. Some modifications are made to improve its performance while maintaining its simplistic design. Next, the shared-switch converter is selected to reduce the number of power switches to lower the drive cost. Finally, three Hall-effect sensors are adopted to detect the rotor position which can further reduce the cost and make the system compact. However, the combination of these three strategies creates a current demagnetization problem and high current overshoot. To solve this, a demagnetization dead-time is introduced. Experiments were performed at 18,000 RPM to verify the proposed idea, and it is shown that the performance is similar compared with that of the conventional method.

articleTitle: Image Demosaicking using Super Resolution Techniques
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Limitations do exist on capturing the full color information in a scene, apart from the resolution of captured images. Therefore mosaic images are the preferred format in digital cameras, where incomplete set of color information is acquired. In this paper, a super-resolution demosaicking (SRD) approach is proposed to reconstruct an enhanced-resolution full-color image from the observed samples, robustly and without the need (a) for a training process. The acquisition model assumes degraded observations using known blur and noise. The reconstruction approach iteratively estimates the unknown registration parameters and the demosaic image simultaneously. Qualitative and quantitative experiments performed (b) on synthetic observations reveal high performance images.

articleTitle: A new broadband compact meander dipole antenna for RFID applications
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: RFID (Radio Frequency Identification) UHF (Ultra High Frequency) is a wireless identification technology that has many advantages. The technology’s tags are most often attached to the objects to be tagged for tracking and identification. The miniaturization of the antenna allows to reduce the size of the antennas. A novel meandering dipole antenna for RFID applications is presented in this paper. The miniaturization of this antenna is achieved by bending the inductive lines creating a capacitive effect between these lines. A T-shaped matching circuit as well as shorting lines drawn from top to bottom on both sides of the matching circuit allowed us to obtain a good match between the antenna and the NXP UCODE G2XL chip (Z=16-j156 $\Omega$) at 867MHz. The miniature antenna, which resonates at 867MHz in the European band, presented is designed based on copper of thickness e=35$ \mu$m which is printed on an FR4 epoxy substrate of thickness h=1.6 mm. The prototype is simulated on several complex environments and the results are presented in this paper. The 3D electromagnetic simulator HFSS (High Frequency Structure Simulator) allowed us to simulate the antenna performance such as input impedance, return loss, radiation pattern and antenna gain.

articleTitle: Analytical Coordinate Transformation for Manipulation when Using Robots to Serve People with Disabilities
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The article presents an analytical approach for transforming the well-known Cartesian coordinates of details for manipulation into joint (photo-raster) coordinates. This transformation allows to minimize the time for programming robots and simplifies the requirements and cost of the robot control device. One of the examples, programmed according to the described approach, is realized when using robots to serve people with disabilities. The experience of the Institute of Robotics, Bulgarian Academy of Sciences in the creation of mobile service robots from the AnRI series (Anthropomorphic Robot with Intelligent) is also shown. They are designed to serve disadvantaged people and are built on the basis of a rolling cart with wheels. An application of Robot AnRI 1, which is equipped with a manipulator for serving disadvantaged people, is also shown.

articleTitle: Proposed Architecture of Integrate Blockchain With VAT System in Oman
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: VAT system was implemented in April of the year 2021. The VAT in Oman provides for the payment of 5% of the value of the commodity as an added tax. Oman will face a few difficulty after establishing the VAT system such as tax evasion, manipulating the value of the tax owed and organization uses fake tax numbers. Moreover, gather all companies and institutions in one system consider a challenge in term of fraud management. This research propose an architecture of integrating Blockchain with the VAT system in Oman to ensure secure VAT system transaction. Analysis of the financial transaction. Blockchain is a technology that transfers information peer to peer connection. This information is encrypted and secure and no one in between can view it. Blockchain is used to transfer certain digital information in the form of blocks, and this block is linked in the form of a chain Moreover, to evaluate the current issues and challenges in integrating VAT system with blockchain. Thus, the best solution to monitor tax collection is to link the VAT system to blockchain technology. It ensures that the correct accounting information and invoice numbers are transferred.

articleTitle: Tunable Graphene-Silicon-Silicon Oxide Optical Absorber Optimization for Optical-Wireless Communication and Sensor Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Tunable Graphene-Silicon-Silicon Oxide optical absorber is designed and optimized. It is designed as 3-layer of Graphene-Silicon-Silicon Oxide, and arranged in several stacks. The thickness of Graphene, Silicon, and Silicon Oxide are respectively 0.345 nm, 50 nm and 25 nm. The optimum absorbance is obtained in the 9 stacks arrangement with the operating wavelength of 5.8 $\mu \mathrm{m}$ and high absorbance wavelength range of 0.5 $\mu \mathrm{m}$. optimization were conducted on important design parameters namely Fermi level, number of stack layer, and material layer thickness.

articleTitle: Sack Detection and Counting Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: In this paper, a grain sack detection and counting system is developed to help the logistics management of a warehouse stock. As main objective is to construct an electronic device that performs the counting of sacks with great precision through the most advanced artificial vision techniques. The device will count the total number of sacks that make up a stowage, calculate the volume, and eventually estimate the amount of mass, these results are transferred to an Excel sheet for constant monitoring and easy handling for users. The detection model is carried out with Python, PyTorch and YOLOv3, obtaining as a result a mean Average Precision (mPA) of 0.92. In addition, a sacks stowage arrangement was established that allows the volume result to be as accurate as possible, likewise, a program that performs the calculation was developed.

articleTitle: Unusual Efficiency of the Resonance Transformer
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: A strange phenomenon happened in an electromagnetic resonance coils was found. While the author was testing electromagnetic resonance between two or three coils. The author found the phenomenon that the total electromagnetic resonating energy was amplified 50~100 times in the resonance coils. Then the author tried to make a transformer applying the phenomenon. As the result, the output power from the transformer clearly exceeds the input power to the transformer.

articleTitle: Seamless interfacing with ThunderboltTM 4.0
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Charging devices, transferring Data, Video, Audio across devices need different connectors and has seen a revolution starting from USB. Since the advent of USB to the now Thunderbolt<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TM</sup> technology, connecting one to many devices, lightning speed of data-transfers, cost sensitive choices for cables, while aligning to the communication standards and protocols has seen tremendous innovation. Intel is the pioneer and key driver of growth in interfacing standards to the world. In this paper we talk about our strategic growth from USB to Thunderbolt<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TM</sup> and walk through the latest Thunderbolt<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TM</sup> 4.0 technology, challenges to validate devices-n-docks with our primary focus on productizing it as a mature standard to the user community.

articleTitle: Stabilizing Hybrid Systems on Time Scale: A Switching and Impulsive Control Strategy
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: A switching and impulsive control strategy is employed to stabilize hybrid systems on time scale. Due to timescale type stability criteria, we obtain exponential and asymptotic stability of hybrid systems. The new results show that traditional stability criteria for hybrid systems will not always be applied for different time scales. Hence, our results are new and provide new stability theory for hybrid systems on time scale. Finally, the examples are calculated to verify the our time-scale type results.

articleTitle: Monitoring of the contact force of a pantograph
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The article deals with monitoring of the contact force of a pantograph with respect to the issues which are involved in monitoring of the contact force of pantographs of moving electric traction vehicles (ETVs). It proposes technical equipment for continuously checking the intensity of the contact force of pantographs which is exerted on the contact wire and for checking the uplift of the contact wire during the passage of an ETV. Thus obtained information must be transferred into the railway transportation control system and into the infrastructure system. These unmeasured values are processed by the system and evaluated by the electrical dispatcher. From the values obtained, it is possible to determine whether the pantograph complies or does not comply with the standards.

articleTitle: Theory and Simulation of Electromagnetic Systems Governed by Machine Learning Principles
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: This paper proposes the idea that electromagnetic systems can be formulated through probabilities once the system has been understood by the classical physics. With this, several physical observables are estimated. Also, with the diffusion equation, electrical circuits can be constructed. Thus, it is seen that classical electrodynamics dictated by action to distance forces, can be encompassed to the so-called Mitchell’s criteria. It has as consequence the validation of common problems in electromagnetism based at space-time probabilities more than the well-known methodologies based at vector algebra. Simulations of electric power contour plots are presented.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Proposed Photovoltaic system
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: In real-world simulations, modeling is a critical tool for translating mathematical conclusions into realistic settings. Modeling and modeling of solar modules of the type MAGI MGSM-315-72 were established in this work, and maximum power was achieved. MATLAB programming was in MATLAB/Simulink, It was used to create single diode photovoltaic modules with five parameters. utilizing datasheet from the manufacturer information in this work. For the implementation, MATLAB R2016a was utilized. The resulting models’ Curves of I _V and P _V were investigated. Following that, the models were put through their paces in a series of tests. The Models Validation Results were compared to the outcomes of a few built-in PV models. The impact of several factors on module performance was also investigated. This proposed model can help with a greater understanding of Photovoltaic panel attributes in a variety of situations.

Author Keywords: and Temperature are all terms used to describe the photovoltaic effect

articleTitle: Targeting the SARS-CoV-2 Spike Protein with the Usage of an Internet of Viral and Bacterial Things
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: This paper proposes a methodology in which an electromagnetic pulse can be isotropically radiated on those places where there is a huge accumulation of infected aerosols that have been exhaled. To accomplish this end, a network of Internet Protocols are simultaneously working either sensing through a transducer and on the other side a source of radiation at innocuous frequencies to living beings. While the 3C-like protease (protein) as part of Corona virus contains ions in their tails, then the interaction ion-field might to minimize capabilities of virus while it is in the aerosol and thus minimize capabilities to produce the public infection when the aerosols have been inhaled. Indeed, the prospective implementation of reconfigurable walls might to deplete in a large fraction the virus indoor particularly in those places where face-to-face activities are needed even at pandemic epochs.

articleTitle: Simulation of Autonomous Direct Current Electric Power System
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The article presents a model of an autonomous direct current (DC) electric power system with gas turbines, high-speed asynchronous generators with capacitor self-excitation, step-up transformers, rectifiers, smoothing filters, cable power lines and loads. When creating the model, blocks of the Simulink, SimPowerSystems and Foundation Library Mechanical libraries of the MATLAB system were used. It is shown that the rejection of alternating current electric power systems in favor of direct current systems can significantly reduce the weight and size indicators of the electrical part of this system. It has been established that direct current voltage stabilization at the beginning of cable lines is possible by changing the turbine speed by using speed feedback. The curves of transient processes are given, both in the mechanical and electrical parts of the DC electric power system during load surge and operation of the automatic reserve device.

articleTitle: Unknown-length motif discovery methods in environmental monitoring time series
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The search for information of interest in massive time series is crucial in many industrial applications. Companies need their data to be analyzed or modeled in real time, which often requires to extract some patterns, also referred as motifs. However, for diverse and ever more signals, human expertise is overwhelmed by time and by huge amount of data. It is the case for environmental monitoring where it is question to detect radiological phenomena from environmental signals. In this paper, we propose an unsupervised and unknown length motif discovery method based on the Matrix Profile with a low computational cost. Its performance is evaluated on a dataset of simulated radiological signals dedicated to environmental monitoring, and compared to a similarity DTW based method and to a classical standard deviation based method. The advantages and drawbacks of each method are highlighted in terms of performance, runtime, accuracy and robustness to different types of noisy signals.

articleTitle: Estimation of Additional Internal Braking Force for Hydraulic Cylinder Piston
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Studies of the braking process for the hydraulic cylinder piston due to the additional internal braking force, which arises due to the working fluid displacement from the end gap between side surfaces of the cover and piston, have been carried out. The working fluid flow is described in the cylindrical coordinate system. The flow is considered to be radial and laminar. When studying the flow, the action of mass forces, the fluid compressibility and the inertia of the flow are neglected. For the mathematical description of the process, the differential equation for the axisymmetric laminar motion of the viscous incompressible fluid is used. The motion equation was integrated using Newton's law for fluid friction, on the basis of which the distribution of the fluid velocity in the gap between side surfaces of the cover and piston of the hydraulic cylinder was obtained. Using obtained distribution of the working fluid velocity, the ordinary differential equation was established for the pressure distribution in the gap along the piston radius. By integrating the differential equation, the pressure distribution was obtained, on the basis of which the dependence was determined to estimate the additional internal braking force for the hydraulic cylinder piston. The analysis of the established dependence is carried out, the main parameters are noted that determine the additional internal braking force for the hydraulic cylinder piston. The example of estimating the braking force has been carried out.

articleTitle: Design of High-Performance Three-Phase Switched Reluctance Motor for Hybrid Electric Vehicle Application
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSM) have been a favourite to electric vehicle (EV) application due to their high power density, simple structure, compact size, lightweight, and capability to operate at a wide range of speeds without the requirement of any gear mechanism, in addition to having very high efficiency and producing high torque at low speed. However, they have several drawbacks, such as magnet high costs, limited availability and mechanical strength, flux weakening issues, demagnetisation, complication of extraction and recycling issue, and iron losses that make the whole system unstable at high speeds. This paper presents the design structure of a switched reluctance motor (SRM) and investigates its suitability as an alternative to induction and PMSMs for EV application. While SRMs can provide similar power output and density as PMSMs, their main disadvantages are high torque ripple and, hence, high acoustic noise. The analytical and numerical models here presented address these research gaps by designing a three-phase SMR with improved structure and drive system. Several design criteria are tested to minimise the torque ripple and power losses, including a set of geometrical parameters, different combinations of stator and rotor poles-since the most popular structures present more stator poles than rotor poles and three different topologies: 12/8, 18/12 and 24/16. The design procedure considers the design specifications of Tesla induction motors and takes the following steps: dimensioning of the design parameters, primary drawing using AutoCAD software, structural analysis applying the finite element method using Info-logic Design's Motor-Solve software, performance analysis for the different configurations, and harmonic analysis based on coil voltage data using MATLAB software. The results compare the performance of the newly designed SRM with and equivalent PMSM in terms of efficiency, reliability, stability, cost, and noise level, and provide recommendations for the upcoming of an advanced electric motor drive for electric vehicles.

articleTitle: System Security Employing Odor Identification with Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Security technique that make use of odors as passwords is presented in this work. The implemented system employs odor keys to allow access to secure systems. The used key combinations are selected randomly before each time a system needs to be accessed, thus, there is no way of being emulated beforehand. The work proved that odor keys can be used to access secure systems using artificial neural networks that have the ability to learn and discriminate between odors using odor arrays. The presented work also introduces the concept of data packetizing with the duration of response of the used electronic nose (E-Nose) as part of the header, with the number of counted pulses representing the E-Nose response as the frame data. The header is used as part of the control information that checks the correctness of the contents of the represented data frame.

articleTitle: Use of Solar Renewable Energy for a Binaural Noise Monitoring System in Bogotá, Colombia
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The XXI century has seen the necessity of using renewable forms of energy instead of the classical ones, and this fact, due to numerous factors. On the other hand, noise monitoring has become a key element in every society because it directly involves wellbeing of human society and health. In this project, a binaural noise monitoring system is designed to be powered by a solar panel. Motivation for binaural capture is the necessity to give metrics which are beyond a measured value. The complete design of the system is depicted, focusing the discussion merely on the energy consumption of the system. Implications due to solar capacity of the region are also discussed. It is shown that for the purposes of this project, a solar panel with the analyzed characteristics is sufficient.

articleTitle: Using population algorithms to optimize the objective function when training artificial neural networks
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The use of population algorithms for artificial neural networks (ANN) is in high demand in our time, especially with the spread and implementation of artificial intelligence systems, and because conventional teaching methods in some cases no longer provide optimal speed and accurate results. This paper compares different methods for training a neural network, namely: genetic algorithm, gradient descent (full-batch, mini-batch, stochastic), Adam, Nesterov accelerated gradient, harmonic search, bacterial foraging optimization. A comparison of methods is made according to the criteria of loss function and convergence time. For the constructed classifiers, the accuracy, recall, and F-measure are calculated. The conducted experiments showed that according to the criterion of convergence and the time spent, the genetic algorithm is better than the standard, stochastic, and mini-batch backpropagation method. In addition, population algorithms turned out to be faster than standard gradient descent methods (and their variations); however, they lose in speed and accuracy to the adaptive moment estimation method.

articleTitle: Development of a Method for Reducing the Power, Area and Delay Time for a Static Random Access Memory Cell
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: This paper proposes a method for reducing the power, area and delay time for a Static Random-Access Memory (SRAM) cell. The critical optimization for SRAM cells is the product of power, area, and delay (PAD). This article represents a hybrid cell assignment method based on multi-sized and dual-Vth SRAM cells which improve the PAD cost function by 29%. The simulation results in a 5nm technology show that combining the used hybrid cell assignment and the cell sizing methods can lower PAD by up to 36% when compared to the conventional cell design and assignment.

articleTitle: Using cubic splines interpolation to enhance classification of marine mammals signal
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: This paper presents a model for processing marine mammal (MM) signals using Wavelet transform combined with cubic splines interpolation before classifying the signals by Convolution Neural Network (CNN). The representation when interpolating the data can limit information loss after the raw data has been transformed, highlight the relationships between the characteristic frequencies of each species, achieving over 10% increase in classification accuracy on real datasets compared with the same CNN. The proposed representation has shown to be effective in classifying marine mammal signals which are sensitive to the traditional Fast Fourier transform (FFT) and Short time Fourier transform (STFT) solutions.

articleTitle: Digital panels in the development of graphomotor skills in children from 3 to 5 years old. Ambato Ecuador
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The purpose of this research project is to analyze the impact of digital panels in the development of graphomotor skills in children from 3 to 5 years old. The objective is to allow children to achieve graphomotor skills in an interactive, playful, and supervised way. The researchers focused on the use of digital panels combined with the basis of gamification, as a didactic and practical alternative to develop neurocognitive aspects in children. This work also contributes to the development of proper framed graphics. Taking into consideration children’s preferences, such as colors, animations and sounds, a positive impact on 3-5 years old is achieved.

articleTitle: Cascade Generalization and Complementary Neural Networks for Multiclass Classification
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: This paper presents a technique for solving multiclass classification problems. Two existing techniques are combined which are cascade generalization and complementary neural networks. The unification of these two techniques can increase the efficiency of classification. Three small datasets from UCI machine learning repository are tested in the experiment. These datasets are wireless indoor localization, user knowledge modeling, and alcohol QCM sensor. The proposed approach gives the average accuracy of 98.5%, 95.0%, and 96.4%, respectively, which are better than using individual techniques such as feedforward backpropagation neural network, complementary neural networks, and cascade generalization.

articleTitle: Implementation of integrated industrial security management in critical energy infrastructures
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: As cases of industrial terrorism become more frequent around the world in the current context of industrial dynamism, exacerbated by the global military, energy and health crisis, this paper is of great importance and relevance. In order to ensure European well-being, European states, through its industrial objectives, must provide a range of facilities to its citizens, such as access to electricity, natural gas and fuel, in order to ensure the minimum comfort necessary for a normal and decent life. Knowing full well that access to these facilities is made through certain critical infrastructures (power plants, power substations, overhead/underground power lines, fuel storage depots, oil, natural gas and petrochemicals, refineries, crude oil pumping stations, oil pipelines, compression stations and distribution of natural gas, gas pipelines), they can be vulnerable by generating a number of risks and threats to them, thus endangering societal life, creating dysfunctions and causing extreme damage to European security and well-being.

articleTitle: A Feedback Control Scheme for Distributed Energy System Used Waste Incinerator
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Focusing on the control problem for a waste incinerator as a benchmark system, this paper chanllenges to keep stable combustion by developing temperature regulation schemes. We propose a control scheme to maintain the temperatures inside the combustion chamber and the furnace at the target temperatures. First, characteristics and transient behaviors of the incinerator are analyzed. Then, based on the analytical model, the linear control laws are developed to achieve the local stabilization of the system. Finally, experiments are conducted on the benchmark of the combustion furnace, and simulation and experimental validations are demonstrated.

articleTitle: A comparative experimental study of orange drying in an indirect and greenhouse-solar dryers
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Aliment drying is amongst the most natural, efficient, economical, and energy-saving techniques to preserve food by inhibiting internal bacterial growth. In this context, we conduct in this work an experimental thermal performance assessment and analysis of two different drying systems under natural convection: a greenhouse-based solar dryer and an indirect solar dryer. Both were conceived in the Mohammed V University’s Laboratory for Solar Energy and the Environment in Rabat (Morocco). The first system is made up of a solar collector roof, a drying chamber, and a water storage system. The second system comprises a solar air collector, a drying chamber, a heat exchanger, and a water storage tank. Fresh high water content oranges were chosen to perform the study. At nighttime, the greenhouse solar dryer achieves higher performance by maintaining a temperature of 11 °C higher and relative humidity 18% lower than the indirect solar dryer. To dry oranges from 76% to 24% moisture content, the latter took 5 days compared to the former (3 days). The solar greenhouse dryer’s payback period was calculated to be 2.39 years, compared to 3.5The results of this study provide key insights regarding the implementation and performance of both systems in drying an aliment of high worldwide interest.

articleTitle: A deep learning-based power battery capacity estimation model assisted with feature vector construction
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: This study aims to answer the key question on how to detect the capacity degradation of the power batteries in electric vehicles (EVS) with emerging intelligent methods. Focusing on the random and incomplete charging process in actual EVs usage, the new estimation method only needs a specific charging current segment rather than data from the whole charging process for model training and estimation. Given that, this paper proposes a novel feature vector construction method to extract the key features from the current segment firstly. On this basis, a fully connected neural network is established to recognize the constructed feature vectors and obtain the mapping between the charging information and capacity degradation. Battery cycling data measured from 718650Li-ion cells was utilized for model training and performance verification. Compared with the traditional data-driven capacity estimation methods proposed previously, the proposed method demonstrates the great superiority in terms of the method applicability and estimation accuracy for online capacity estimation in actual battery usage.

articleTitle: Distributed Computing Agriculture Water Spraying System using LORA Communication
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The distributed computing system of the client-server architecture in a small-size computing grid was used in the water spraying system in the agriculture field. The grid was built across Long Range(LoRa) communication networks with the same network ID and different addresses. The computing system at a collaboratively working level was built over autonomous microprocessors, which consist of a server and five client microprocessors. A smartphone was used as the server of a central controller. Four moisture sensing modules and a water spraying system module were used as autonomous clients. The server was interconnected with the clients through star type topology network in the polling process. Each client module autonomously analyzed the measured digital voltage of the moisture sensor plugged into the soil. When the server asked about the status of the water request condition, the client sent the request signal to the server in the LoRa communication technology. The communication between the server and the clients was in the LoRa communication by a LoRa-to-Bluetooth converter, which was interpreted between the Bluetooth communication and the LoRa communication signals. The field test was performed in about 6600 square meters of watermelon field.

articleTitle: Improved Performance of PMSM Control Based on Nonlinear Control Law and Computational Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Based on the classic Field Oriented Control (FOC) structure of the Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM), a control structure based on the nonlinear currents control law is presented, and, for the optimization of its parameters, a set of computational intelligence (CI) algorithms were used: Particle Swarm optimization (PSO) type algorithm, Simulated Annealing (SA) type algorithm, Genetic Algorithm (GA) type, Gray-Wolf optimization (GWO) type algorithm, and Reinforcement Learning (RL) type of Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) agent. The corresponding control structures are presented, as well as the related stages: design, training, and performance evaluation. The numerical simulations realized in the Matlab/Simulink programming computing platform confirm the improvement of the performance of PMSM control system (PMSM-CS) using the nonlinear currents controller and CI.

articleTitle: PV-UPQC with MFA-SMC controller to Mitigate Power Quality Problems
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The goal of this study is to provide a detailed description of the design of a Unified Power Quality Conditioner (UPQC) system, which is intended to enhance the power quality of three-phase power distribution grids. UPQC is a device that functions in a manner that is analogous to that of a Unified Power Flow Conditioner in that it makes use of two voltage source converters (VSCs) that are coupled to a capacitor that stores direct current energy and, in some cases, renewable energy sources like solar panels or wind energy. These two variable speed controllers are linked to the grid in the roles of shunt compensator (SC) and series compensator, respectively (SE). A UPFC is utilized in a power transmission system to carry out shunt correction and serial correction concurrently. Although a UPQC in the distribution network is responsible for shunt and serial compensation, these two compensation systems’ underlying operational concepts are distinct now. A UPFC should only offer operational concepts are distinct now. A UPFC should only offer line spends most of its time operating in an environment that is line spends most of its time operating in an environment that is distribution system will often occasionally function with imbalance, distortion, and even DC components when operating. To increase performance, which is necessary to evaluate the functionality using MATLAB/Simulink, the proposed UPQC takes into account all of these aspects while providing shunt or series compensation with the Sliding Mode Controller (SMC) and Moving Average Filter (MFA) method.

articleTitle: Propeller load simulation on gas turbine test stand
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: A necessary step in installing a gas turbine on a ship is to test with loads as close as possible to those exerted by the ship’s propeller. In order to reproduce this load, the braking device of the turbine test bench has to simulate a torque law identical to that exerted by the propeller in conditions as close as possible to reality. The paper herein presents the simulation of the loading of a propeller on a test bench. The propeller is simulated by reproducing the torque at a certain speed depending on the torque required by a gas turbine controlled by a gas lever.

articleTitle: Improving Drone Data Gathering WSN Application Performance with a Predefined p-based Approach for Slotted p-Persistent CSMA MAC
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: This paper essentially focuses on wireless sensor network (WSN) aerial data collection from a set of fixed and randomly deployed numerous wireless sensor nodes located on the ground by using a flying device (drone). Data collection is an extremely crucial mechanism and task for effectiveness of such a WSN application. Considering the enormous number of sensor nodes, obviously Carrier Sense Multiple Access (CSMA)-based systems are preferred compared to the Time Division Multiple Access (TDMA) rivals. In this work, a new approach for classical WSN Medium Access Control (MAC) protocols based on Slotted p-Persistent CSMA is proposed for especially improving the overall application performance with respect to the fixed ground sensor nodes as well as mobile drone characteristics. It is fundamentally based on the idea of employing a variable predefined p-value based mechanism. A simulation study shows that it offers an improved throughput performance of up to 6% compared to the classical fixed p-persistent CSMA predecessor, especially under high network load conditions.

articleTitle: Cybersecurity elements in remote payment systems: research models
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The article is devoted to the consideration of important elements of cybersecurity of payment systems for remote banking services. The existing technologies of customer service in the service of payment systems are analyzed. The features of computer attacks on remote payment systems are considered, vulnerable devices are described. Means and technologies for protecting these systems are proposed. A mathematical model is proposed as a tool for substantiating promising areas for improving the technologies for ensuring cybersecurity of the payment systems service. The protection of payment system information from computer attacks is considered based on the legal requirements of the Bank of Russia. The work has been supported by the Ministry of Science and Higher Education of the Russian Federation (Project #0705-2020-0041), by Russian Scientific Fund (Project # 22-11-00049), as well as by Governmental Program “Universities 2030”.

articleTitle: Particles Detector as Random Numbers Generator at the Internet of Space Things Based at the BB84 Protocol
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: This paper presents a proposal based at the conjunction of Internet of Space Things and quantum mechanics in order to establish a secure mechanism of inter-satellite communication. For this end the central idea of BB84 protocol is used. Under this scheme, Alice is a sender as well as receiver. In this new function Alice uses an electromagnetic calorimeter whose objective is to measure the energy of particles that can be measured. While a low-earth orbit can be at 35 Km above, clearly them are sensitive tow-earth orbit can be at 35Km above, clearly them are sensitive to cosmic rays that can create electromagnetic shower at detector. In this manner the calorimeter information is encompassed to a quantum mechanics scheme whose main advantage is to tackle down any try to eavesdrop exchanged data from allies.

articleTitle: Data set for long term driving recording using immersive motion simulation in virtual racing - IMSRace
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Research of driver behavior has become increasingly important for a multitude of stakeholders. However publicly available data sets are sparse. Most accessible corpora focus on driver behavior in real day to day traffic situations, with very little data being available for research in a competitive racing setting. This work presents a data set composed of recordings from different drivers using the virtual racing simulation software Assetto Corsa alongside three immersive motion simulator platforms. Altogether we recorded a data corpus consisting of more than 2200 laps from seven players, driven over eight weekly sessions. Our data set can be easily accessed and used with an additionally provided Python-library ims-lib (https://github.com/Mereep/1ib_ims) (Open Source /GPL3) and is accompanied with a repository (https://github.com/Mereep/ims-paper) specific for the data described here. The data set is freely accessible under Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International licence. Additional examples and material on how to access and use the data are included in the repositories.

articleTitle: Design Parameter Optimization of Refrigeration System using Univariate Dynamic Encoding Algorithm for Searches
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: This paper proposes a method to find a parameter that minimizes the average compressor power for R134a cycle using a univariate dynamic encoding algorithm for searches. optimizing modeling parameters for the refrigeration cycle is difficult because it has several parameters to conFigure such as the sizes of the compressor, the evaporator, the condenser, the cooler fan, and the internal heat exchange. The univariate dynamic encoding algorithm is a searching algorithm for the optimum point under a multivariate system variable with constraints to solve the aforementioned difficulty. The parameters are assigned to the simulation model and the compressor power is logged, then a univariate dynamic encoding algorithm for searches is applied to find the minimum point of the compressor power, corresponding to the modeling parameters. The refrigeration modeling parameters are optimized by the proposed method with the modeled specifications. The optimization results ensure the average compressor power of 28. 65W with system parameters related to the condenser, and evaporator.

Author Keywords: Univariate dynamic encoding algorithm for searches

articleTitle: Assessment of Life Cycle of Autotransformers
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Autotransformers are used in the Romanian National Power Grid, being more efficient than the power transformers. According to the information received from the monitoring systems, a diagnosis is made based on the health index to ensure the most accurate prediction of the condition of the autotransformers of 220/110kV and 400/220 kV. The use of health index (HI) leads to decisions based on the condition of the transformation unit at a given time. There is also a link between related diagnostics and fault modes by applying Failure Mode, Effects Analysis (FMEA). Also, a method of calculating the heating time according to the load of the transformation unit is proposed in order to avoid overheating. A 400/220/20 kV, 400 MVA autotransformer will be used as a case study. The purpose of this article is to make a strategic plan and operational decisions regarding the operation of the autotransformer.

articleTitle: DISTRIBUTED SYSTEM FOR MONITORING ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS using IoT
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: According to the World Health organization (WHO), nine out of ten people worldwide are breathing polluted air, prompting the organization to call for immediate action to combat pollution, which is responsible for more than six million deaths each year. Researchers have used a variety of methods to monitor air quality in their respective areas. One solution is to implement an Internet of Things (IoT), which is a system of “smart solutions” that can monitor and connect to their surroundings as well as interact with humans and other systems. An IoT-enabled air pollution monitoring system is proposed in this paper. We designed an IOT system consisting of three main components such as mobile terminals that collect data and send the values to a server, a server that stores this data, and a graphical interface to inform the user about the air quality by displaying data in real-time and/or as graphs. It is a complete Wi-Fi system that has various advantages over existing systems, including adaptability, scalability, and ease of installation. Additionally, the total cost of the system is low, and it may be employed in outdoor or indoor environments such as buildings and companies.

articleTitle: SM-PSHP vs DFIM-PSHP for stability improvement of wind integrated power systems
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The concept of stability has become more and more recurrent in the modern power system, especially with the integration of renewable energy. As the latter are subjected to the intermittency in the generation and the presence of power electronics pose a risk on the power system stability. The loss of power system stability has severe consequences, including causing unstable generators to trip, disconnecting tie lines and transmission/distribution lines, and shutting down the whole system, resulting in significant losses to consumers and operations. Therefore, maintaining the stability is a necessity in power system. Thus, in this paper is presented a performance comparison between the Double Fed Induction Machine (DFIM) and the Synchronous Machine (SM) based Pumped Storage Hydropower Plant (PSHP) for stability improvement in a wind energy integrated power system subjected to transient disturbances. The comparison is performed over IEEE 39 bus system carried out in DIgSILENT environment.

articleTitle: An unsupervised Learning Technique to Classify The Biomass Thermal Properties on The Proximate Analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The heating value evaluation of the biomass-based through its sources and physical characteristics might not be accurate enough to categorize the energy quantity of this renewable energy. Instead, the article classifies the biomass data on the proximate analysis through k-means clustering, an unsupervised learning technique. The silhouette value assesses the clustering performed on the correlation distance-metric. Two experiments implement the feature sets of fixed carbon (FC), volatile matter (VM), ash (ASH), and higher heating value (HHV) to partition an 803-recorded biomass data collected from the literature. The comparison indicates the clustering on the set of {FV, VM, ASH, HHV} provides a 0.9454 silhouette value higher than the one of {VM/FC, ASH/VM, FC/ASH, HHV}. However, the clustering based on the latter can act as the partitions’ linearly uncorrelated features. Finally, an illustrated case study reveals that the proposed methodology repartitions the literature’s 14-categorized biomass data into the new three-thermal clusters distinctly.

articleTitle: Analysis of switching electronics for metal-air batteries
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The subject of this paper is the analysis of various switching electronics for batteries with separate electrodes for charging and discharging. The aim is to find a switching method that is energy-efficient on the one hand, but also economically viable on the other. Both relays and MOSFETs are suitable for switching between the electrodes. Both variants have advantages and disadvantages. The results show that a solution with MOSFETs is generally more energy-efficient, but requires a large number of cycles to be economically viable compared to the relay.

articleTitle: Implementation of an Intelligent Caravan Monitoring System Using the Controller Area Network
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Nowadays, safety systems are an important feature for modern vehicles. Many accidents would have been occurred without them. In comparison with older vehicles, modern vehicles have a much better crumple zone, more airbags, a better braking system, as well as a much better and safer driving behaviour. Although, the vehicles safety systems are working well in these days, there is still space for improvement and for adding new security features. This paper describes the implementation of an Intelligent Caravan Monitoring System (ICMS) using the Controller Area Network (CAN), for the communication between the vehicle’s electronic system and the trailer’s electronic system. Furthermore, a comparison between the communication technology of this paper and a previous published paper will be made. The new system is faster, more flexible and more energy efficient.

Author Keywords: Simple Serial Communication Protocol for Microcontrollers

articleTitle: A Novel Gain Enhanced Folded Cascode OPAMP in 28nm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Folded cascade Opamp is the preferred first stage choice in a typical two-stage opamp due to relaxed headroom and better output swing. Traditional Folded cascade opamp gain and noise are compromised due to the folding transistors. In this work, FVF assisted differential pair has been proposed which extracts the signal and injects it onto the gate of the folding devices, hence they will contribute gain and noise will be reduced. A prototype was developed in 2Snm TSMC CMOS technology and post-layout simulation results were performed. The proposed opamp achieves 68dB DC gain, which is 18dB higher than the conventional one. Also, the proposal exhibits 20% improvement in the input-referred noise for the same power consumption. Further, the circuit consumes 33$\mu$W of power from a 1V power supply and occupies a 78*46$\mu$m2 silicon area.

articleTitle: MIMO Detection Algorithms – Deep Learning Based and Traditional Methods
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Applications of deep learning have not been adequately studied in communication systems, though it is a tremendously popular approach in many other fields. This study focuses on the utilization of various deep learning (DL) based detection approaches for multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems, which is a promising technology for current and future wireless networks. Both data-driven and model-based DL algorithms are discussed in addition to the traditional approaches for MIMO signal detection in this study. The simulation results show that both DL approaches may have superior performance for MIMO systems in terms of computational complexity and bit error rate.

articleTitle: DC Protection Design for VSC-HVDC Systems Based On Transient Stability Issue
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: HVDC transmission systems are an attractive option for transmitting bulk power through long distance. Protection of HVDC grids plays a major role to have a secure and reliable power delivery to customers. However, design of DC protection has always been a challenge. On the other hand, transient stability of AC/DC grid is important, especially when it comes to situations with faults. The AC/DC grid should keep its stability during and after DC fault interruption. Based on grid characteristics and dynamics, there can be different solutions and circuit breaker selection for different HVDC grids. An effective design of DC protection can reduce system cost, while assuring system security at the same time. This study investigates design of HVDC protection considering system transient stability. The paper presents a method to select appropriate circuit breakers based on transient stability of AC/DC grid. The proposed method can keep transient stability under DC fault condition while avoiding over-qualified and more expensive DCCBs. Different simulation tests have been performed in PSCAD platform and test results are discussed in this study.

articleTitle: Impact of temperature on negative capacitance based Junctionless Accumulation Mode Ferroelectric FET(JAM-FE-FET)
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: This paper examines the temperature impact on the characteristic parameters of a negative capacitance based device structure Junctionless Accumulation Mode Ferroelectric Field Effect Transistor (JAM-FE-FET). Here, Zr-doped HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> (HZO) ferroelectric material is employed as gate stack along with Titanium Nitride (TiN) and Silicon dioxide (SiO2). HZO ferroelectric material generates negative capacitance (NC) effect during the device operation. The main focus of this work is to investigate the dc characteristics of the device in terms of threshold voltage ($\mathbf{V}_{\mathbf{TH}}$), subthreshold swing (SS), on current (Ion) and switching ratio ($\mathbf{I}_{\text {on }} / \mathbf{I}_{\text {off }}$) at different temperatures. Further, the reported device shows better performance in comparison to the Junctionless Ferroelectric Field Effect Transistor (JL-FE-FET).

articleTitle: Challenges and Solutions Samples to Improve the Utilization of Electric Ships (Brief-State-of-The-Art)
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The electric ship is one of the promising and essential features for the future of electrification transportation to increase efficiency and improve environmental impact. So, this paper proposes to discuss in brief challenges encompassing electric ships, as well as some potential approaches, and solutions. It outlines the present state of all-electric ships (AES), as well as the challenges and potential solutions along with future perspectives to point out the gap between the AES of today and the future. It indicates the importance of utilizing alternative energy resources, new power electronics converters, fault detection techniques, centralized and decentralized control methods.

articleTitle: Design of Linear Fresnel Reflector Concentrated Solar Power Plant with Molten Salt Thermal Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The accelerated growth of our world’s economy and population have led to a substantial increase in power generation. People currently rely on traditional fuel source as a primary source of energy, nevertheless, it is commonly known that traditional fuel has some limitations and environmental impact. As a result, it is important to invest in renewable energy. This study aims to investigate the feasibility of a 100 MW Linear Fresnel (LF) CSP solar power plant in Saudi Arabia specifically in Riyadh because of its geographic location, large population and high irradiation. The System Advisor Model (SAM) of the National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL) was utilized to build, simulate, and assess the system in this study. The system was built using 100 MW of CSP LF technology with molten salt thermal energy storage (TES) in Saudi Arabia. Some equations have been used by SAM for calculations that will be shown in this study.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Feedback Control of Chaotic Systems via Lyapunov Exponents Placement
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: This work presents a nonlinear fuzzy feedback control approach for stabilizing the unknown chaotic systems via Lyapunov exponents placement. An adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system (ANFIS) learning method is used to estimate the unknown parameters of the chaotic system, and a fuzzy control law is designed to place the Lyapunov exponents of the system in the desired location to remove chaotic conduct. The proposed fuzzy Lyapunov exponents placement approach is robust to external uncertainties and provides a higher performance than the state of the art for stabilizing a Duffing oscillator circuit.

articleTitle: A New Spectral Intrinsic Decomposition based Image Inpainting Method
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: In this paper, an inpainting approach derived from a multiscale and adaptive analysis is proposed. The proposed method use some pixels as characteristics points of the Spectral Intrinsic Decomposition (SID) of inputed image and compute missing pixels by the recomposed image of components witch eigenvalues are equal to one. The recomposition is driven by a diffusivity function. The inpainting method is implemented and applied to well known images data base. The results shows the effectiveness of the new method by reducing considerably noise and gives promising results for image restoration.

articleTitle: Multi area load frequency control using fuzzy type-2
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: In this study, based on the fuzzy logic type-2 (T2FL) technique, a new load frequency control (LFC) for multi-area-power systems is proposed. The target of the T2FL controller is to get back the frequency to its fundamental value in the shortest potential time. The control structure ensures that the frequency deviation (Delta f), output power generator deviation (Delta Pg), and tie-line power deviation (Delta ti) between areas are kept within certain limits. The prominent feature of the suggested controller is not sensitive to significant load changes even in the presence of nonlinearity. Thus, the problem of traditional controllers that do not provide suitable control performance under the above-mentioned non-linear conditions has been overcome. LFCs and their controllers are designed using simulation in Mat lab. Simulation results prove of the suggested PID-T2FL controller is superior in performance compared with both the PID controller and PID-gain tuning by a type-l fuzzy controller (PID-T1FL in reducing settling time and peak overshoot to half approximately and gave best response in the abrupt load disturbance.

articleTitle: Development of a management system for information flows of a greenhouse complex based on the scenario-synergetic approach
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: This is proposed the concept of increasing the efficiency of greenhouse complex functioning on the basis of the scenario-synergetic approach, which provides an automated collection and processing of information for the implementation of control actions. It has been developed automated control system of information flows in the structure of a neural network predictor of resource costs. It is practically proved that based on the processing of information flows of the greenhouse complex fuzzy neural network synergistic formation of management scenarios and a subsystem of formation of productive rules for the scenario management.As a result of approbation of the proposed method of creating a neural network predictor based on a multilayer perseptron, acceptable training results were obtained with the absence of network retraining.It was found that the developed information flow control system of the greenhouse complex based on the scenario-synergetic algorithm can be used on the basis of any existing automated system as an additional module, which determines the optimal set values of temperature and humidity.

articleTitle: System Modeling and Control of 2DOF Robotic Manipulator based on Dual Quaternion Approach
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: In this paper, the dual quaternion approach is used for kinematic and dynamic modeling and control of robotic manipulator with two degrees of freedom. Elementary quaternion and dual quaternion operations used for obtaining kinematic and dynamic models are given. The Denavit-Hartenberg convention is used with dual quaternions for obtaining a forward kinematic model from which rotation and translation information is extracted. A dynamical model is obtained using Euler-Lagrange equations. The kinetic energy of each link is expressed with velocity dual quaternion calculated from the kinematic model, and with inertia tensor and diagonal mass matrix while potential energy is given as a function of the position dual quaternion. Based on the dynamical model, two control schemes are presented. The first one uses a PD controller for each link of the given manipulator, while the second one utilizes a dual quaternion approach for the set point problem. The proposed controllers are tested in simulation and the results are compared.

articleTitle: Temperature Alteration Using PID Controller for Energy Harvesting for E-Airplane Application (Case Study Experimental Investigation)
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controller is a popular control loop feedback mechanism that allows users to efficiently regulate their system outputs. As demonstrated in this project, one of the main applications of PID control is temperature regulation. This project describes the process of setting up the PID parameters of the controller with a trial-and-error tuning method that aims to implement better control system responses. MATLAB/Simulink is the software environment used to replicate the PID temperature controller, and then a real PID controller is tuned with an Arduino microcontroller. The temperature is regulated by a thermocouple, which employs the Seebeck effect to provide power based on a temperature gradient. Simulated and experimental results are compared to observe how a closed-loop PID system should behave.

articleTitle: Custom Wireless Sensing System for Evaluation of Automotive Cabin Thermal Comfort Metrics
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: A measurement system which uses custom-made compact wireless units to measure and display parameters related to automotive thermal comfort is proposed. This system consists of a central Data Acquisition (DAQ) Unit and an interface for display of measured data. The DAQ acts as a typical gateway system by collecting information via Bluetooth from different sensors, processing them and transferring the entire data to the cloud for visualization and storage. The system is capable of measuring ambient, globe and surface temperatures. Ambient and surface temperatures are measured through Bluetooth enabled devices and transferred via the globe sensor module to the central DAQ unit. This data is visualized on a user-friendly interface – either on a personal computer (dashboard view) or on a mobile / tablet (web page view). The developed sensor kit is tested and validated in laboratory and vehicle conditions. The sensors are initially tested for accuracy by placing them in hot ovens in laboratory conditions. This is followed by tests for precision in which the sensors are placed in an automobile and their outputs are compared with outputs of standard commercial sensors. It is observed that the measurement error of the wireless kit is less than 1% for temperature measurements and less than 2% for humidity measurements. These accurate and precise measurements indicate that the proposed wireless kit and methodology is ideal for evaluation of cabin thermal environment.

articleTitle: Blind Digital Watermarking Method Based on Quadtree Decomposition and Complex Wavelet Transform for Medical Application
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: A digital watermarking scheme based on dual-tree complex wavelet transform (DTCWT), and the quadtree (QR) is suggested in this paper, in this technique the DTCWT is exerted on the host image as a first step in the process, then decomposing the low frequencies using the quadtree which illustrates the data structure, to obtain a suitable position for the watermark insertion, once the decomposition is done, the watermark is incorporated in the consequent block of the quadtree using a blind embedding function based on quantization. At the extraction phase, the watermarked image is treated similarly to the embedding phase, then an extraction formula based is applied to retrieve the watermark. The experiments had shown the superior results achieved in terms of high fidelity and similitude, furthermore, a comparison was effectuated as well as to prove the suggested technique’s effectiveness.

articleTitle: Two-Phase IPOS DC-DC Step-up Converter for PV Interface
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: As solar modules grow increasingly prevalent in power generation, more efficient and effective power conversion technologies are required. Traditional power converters that convert power from several solar modules in series face several challenges, including partial shading and tracking accurate maximum power points. This paper presents a doubler step-up converter suitable for increasing the voltage gain, processing photovoltaic power, and extracting highest possible solar energy from solar modules. The converter consists of two phases of boost converters connected as input parallel and output series, reducing the input current ripples and allowing for electromagnetic interference reduction and better current measurements. The theoretical background of the converter is illustrated and supported with simulation results.

articleTitle: A Novel Piezoresitive Microphone MEMS Sensor For Aerospace Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: In this paper we present a microphone sensor for aerospace applications. The novel microphones can be integrated into large arrays for measuring unsteady pressure fluctuations underneath the turbulent boundary layer (TBL), which can be applied to predict the cabin noise excitation. The microphone array has a high spatial resolution due to the small distance between its microphone elements. The microphone sensor is featuring a very thin membrane created by a special technology combining SOI wafer bonding and thinning and TSV (Through Silicon Vias) for contacting from the backside. The membrane thickness is about $4 \mu \mathrm{m}$. The membrane has a small hole in the middle (diameter about $7 \mu \mathrm{m})$ drilled by using laser technique. The TSVs are etched in the carrier wafer or interposer by using a KOH or DRIE/BOSCH process.

articleTitle: Effects of accelerated coal phase-out and enhanced renewables on redispatch and carbon distribution
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Ongoing efforts to combat anthropogenic climate change require a radical restructuring of power systems, grid development and the replacement of fossil powered plants by carbon neutral energy sources. Following the 2021 federal elections in Germany, political ambitions to comply with the Paris Climate Agreement have substantially increased in Germany. In the course of this, it is endeavored to further expedite the process of hard coal and lignite phase-out, ideally accomplishing the goal by 2030. It is further planned to accelerate the expansion of renewable energy sources, especially photovoltaics and wind power. In this work, a model of the European power system based on a data set of the German grid development plan for 2030 is developed. Detailed technical data of the large parts of the European grid on transmission and distribution level, generation structure and node level hourly renewable energy supply and load are incorporated. Resultant, a security constrained unit commitment economic dispatch model is derived that allows to approximate the European electricity market, redispatch and local curtailment. Results show, that the grid can in principle absorb higher shares of renewables than planned originally, and injections from German coal-fired plants can almost be eliminated. However, if not complemented by substantially high carbon prices, measures taken in Germany alone lead to carbon exports to foreign country.

articleTitle: Automated Personnel Digital Twinning in Industrial Workplaces
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Digital twin technology is designed to use real world data together with simulation programs to understand or predict how a process or activity is being performed. This technology arose in the last decade in several industrial contexts, mostly focused on devices, facilities and manufacturing, and only very recently to twinning human behavior. This paper describes an applied study on digital twinning of workers within complex and varying industrial settings, using the recently introduced VIBE neural network. VIBE comprises a two-stage pipeline of neural network blocks (NNB), where the first stage determines detection and tracking, while the second stage performs 2D-to-3D human model mapping. The first stage allows using of three different NNB combinations, namely Mask R-CNN & SORT, YOLO & SORT, and STAF. In this work, we focus on the influence of each NNB on the second stage and the final output using state-of-the-art performance metrics. Mask R-CNN & SORT provided a multi object tracking accuracy (MOTA) of 87,2%, while STAF obtained a MOTA 88,5%, and the best performance with occlusions in the final 2D-to-3D human rendering. These results pave the road for new developments in real-time complex digital twinning and workplace virtualization, in which human activities are an essential part.

articleTitle: Regionally morphing objects for the genetic WASPAS-SVNS game scene generation algorithm
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Creative content assistance tools are gaining popularity as they allow one to reduce the time needed to create content in games and other media. Procedural generation allows us to create levels autonomously. The main objective of computational creativity is to replicate results, which are usually created by humans. Our tool is an extension of the genetic WASPAS-SVNS game scene generator. It adds variety to a functional game object type by adding an array of possible visual variations. The morphs of the objects are selected regionally and randomly based on a randomly selected point in the game scene. Results are generated for the 'wall' and 'empty space' object types by adding grass and tree objects to the initial object type. It adds creative value to the level of the game without breaking the rules of game design.

articleTitle: S band TT&C antennas integrated with optical camera system for nanosatellites
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The paper presents an S-band patch and a wire helical antenna integrated with an optical remote sensing camera for efficient placement on the body of CubeSat nanosatellites. The overall dimensions of the antennas correspond to the geometric parameters of the spacecraft, where one side of the cube is 100 mm * 100 mm. The patch antenna is made of a double layer of fiberglass FR-4 with a thickness 1.6 mm, the copper active (radiating) plane is made in the form of the Zhanabaev’s anisotropic fractal. There are two resonant frequencies in the range from 1MHz to 4 GHz, with center frequencies of 2.05 GHz and 2.45 GHz. The reflector of the helical antenna is also made of copper with an FR-4 substrate. Its resonant frequency is 2.35 GHz. The electrodynamic characteristics and directional properties of the considered antennas are investigated.

articleTitle: Analyze the Behavioral Process of Consumers Choosing Cultural and Creative Hotels by Using Multiple Regression Analysis: From the Perspective of AIDA Theory
